jsonld.site_description: Find every civic district that covers a point or address in New Hampshire, and who represents you there.
jsonld.app_description: Click any point in New Hampshire, or search an address, to see every civic district that contains it, and who represents you there — county, legislative and U.S. House districts, cities and towns, school districts and ZIP codes.

layers.label: U.S. House
layers.rank_note: 2 congressional districts — the largest districts New Hampshire carries below the state itself

source.answers: The U.S. House district covering the point, and the representative holding it.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 0 (120th Congressional Districts), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 2 features for New Hampshire, measured 2026-11-10. Layer 4, the 119th Congress's map, draws the same 2 districts, because New Hampshire's map is still the one the state Supreme Court adopted in May 2022, so nothing changes on 3 January 2027 and the builder refuses to write if the two differ before then. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, together with both chambers' maps in one shared topology, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: congress-roster.json, rebuilt weekly by CI from the public-domain unitedstates/congress-legislators dataset — including each member's district office and Washington office.

layers.label: County
layers.rank_note: 10 counties, pre-built from TIGERweb; the instance's offline anchor layer

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — State_County, layer 1, pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 10 features, measured 2026-11-10. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. Each New Hampshire county elects three commissioners, a sheriff, an attorney, a register of deeds, a register of probate and a treasurer, and its budget is voted by the county delegation, the county's own state representatives; no list of the county officers was read in this pass, so the card names the county only. Recorded as gap nh-county-officials.

source.people: nh-senate-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI: the General Court's own member file (gc.nh.gov) first, and Open States' export of current legislators, compiled from the General Court's own pages, when that file cannot be read. Name, party, the senator's legislative e-mail address and a link to the senator's own page. The General Court's site answered nothing from the build sandbox on 2026-11-11, so the first roster is Open States'.

layers.label: School District (Secondary)
layers.rank_note: 8 secondary districts, about 273 km2 of land on average, running the higher grades over part of the elementary districts' ground, drawn from a mirrored tile archive

source.answers: The secondary school district covering the point, where one runs the higher grades over the point's elementary district.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — School, layer 1 (secondary school districts), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 8 features for New Hampshire, measured 2026-11-11, four running grades 9 to 12, two 7 to 12 and two 6 to 12. The unified districts (the Census's placeholder included) and the elementary districts together cover the state's land (14,747 and 8,444 km2, summing to New Hampshire's 23,191 km2 of land, measured 2026-11-11), and the 8 secondary districts lie over part of the elementary districts' ground (2,181 km2), so a reader there is in one elementary and one secondary district at once. One unified record is not a district: the Census files ground no school district covers as "School District Not Defined" (GEOID 3399997, 859 km2 of land, chiefly Coos County's unincorporated grants and purchases), and the card says no school district is defined there.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No list of the districts' school board members was read in this pass — recorded as gap nh-school-board-members.
source.applies: New Hampshire — part of the elementary districts' ground; the layer answers nothing elsewhere.

layers.label: New Hampshire House District
layers.rank_note: 164 base districts that tile the state, each with the floterial district drawn over it where there is one; 400 representatives in 203 districts

source.answers: The State House district covering the point and the representatives it elects, and the floterial district over it, where there is one, with its representatives.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Legislative, layer 2 (2026 State Legislative Districts - Lower), pre-built for the state and shipped with the app; 164 features, measured 2026-11-10: the base districts of the plan the General Court enacted in 2022, which tile the state. Simplified by Douglas-Peucker at a 5 m interval, together with the U.S. House and Senate maps in one shared topology, and refused over an 8 m fidelity ceiling.

NH GRANIT — APB_ElectoralDistricts, layers 8 (2022 House base districts) and 9 (2022 House floterial districts), read at build time only. 39 floterial districts each elect more representatives from two or more whole base districts together; the builder refuses unless every floterial district is exactly the union of the base districts it names, and stamps each base district with the floterial over it. TIGER does not carry the floterial districts.

source.people: nh-house-members.json, rebuilt weekly by CI: the General Court's own member file (gc.nh.gov) first, and Open States' export of current legislators, compiled from the General Court's own pages, when that file cannot be read. Every representative of each of the 203 districts, with party, legislative e-mail address and a link to the member's own page, and each district's seat count from the plan. A district the roster lists with fewer members than it elects is shipped with those listed and the date it was read, and the card says how many are not listed. The General Court's site answered nothing from the build sandbox on 2026-11-11, so the first roster is Open States'.
source.applies: New Hampshire — statewide, all 164 base districts and the 39 floterial districts over 108 of them.

The unified districts (the Census's placeholder included) and the elementary districts together cover the state's land (14,747 and 8,444 km2, summing to New Hampshire's 23,191 km2 of land, measured 2026-11-11), and the 8 secondary districts lie over part of the elementary districts' ground (2,181 km2), so a reader there is in one elementary and one secondary district at once. layers.label: City or Town
layers.rank_note: 259 county subdivisions (13 cities, 222 towns and 24 unincorporated places), about 90 km2 of land on average, drawn from a tile archive mirrored from TIGERweb

source.answers: The city or town containing the point, or the unincorporated place where there is none.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — Places_CouSub_ConCity_SubMCD, layer 1 (county subdivisions), mirrored into a vector-tile archive this site serves (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py); 260 features for New Hampshire, measured 2026-11-11: 13 cities, 221 towns, the town of Livermore, which the Census records as an inactive government, 24 unincorporated places (8 grants, 6 purchases, 4 locations and 6 townships, 23 of them in Coos County) and 1 water record in Rockingham County named "County subdivisions not defined". Every other part of the state is in a city, a town or an unincorporated place, and the Census files each as a county subdivision, so this layer is the state's whole municipal map.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER YET. No statewide roster of New Hampshire's mayors, councils and select boards was read in this pass; the card names the city or town and links nothing it has not verified. Recorded as gap nh-municipal-officeholders.

layers.label: ZIP Code
layers.rank_note: ZIP Code Tabulation Areas inside New Hampshire, drawn from a tile archive of the ones inside the state; the layer hides outside it

source.answers: The ZIP Code Tabulation Area covering the point — the Census Bureau's areal approximation of the USPS delivery routes sharing a ZIP code, not a postal boundary.

boundary.label: U.S. Census TIGERweb — ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, layer 11 of the PUMA/TAD/TAZ/UGA/ZCTA service, mirrored into a vector-tile archive of the ZCTAs inside New Hampshire (scripts/mirror_tiger_tiles.py). ZCTAs carry NO STATE FIELD because they cross state lines, so this is the one TIGERweb layer here fetched by a bounding ENVELOPE rather than STATE='33'. The app's box reaches into Vermont, Maine and Massachusetts, and only the ZCTAs inside New Hampshire are kept in the archive.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a ZIP code is a mail-routing convenience, not a unit of government, so nobody is elected from one. The card says what the boundary actually is rather than leaving a reader to assume it means more.
source.applies: New Hampshire. The layer is hidden outside the state outline, because outside it the Census's point query answers with a neighbouring state's real ZIP code.

layers.label: Police Station
layers.rank_note: nearest police stations by straight-line distance — a point layer, ranked with the other nearest-N layers

source.answers: The three nearest police stations to the point, by straight-line distance, with each one's address.

boundary.label: USGS The National Map — structures layer 53 (Police Stations), queried live at runtime by a bounding envelope through the paged loader. Public domain. Measured 2026-11-11: 282 points in New Hampshire's envelope, which reaches into Vermont, Maine and Massachusetts; the service caps a page at 2,000 records, so the loader pages.

source.people: NO OFFICEHOLDER, AND NONE IS MISSING: a police station is a facility, not an elected district. Nobody is elected from one.
source.applies: New Hampshire — plus the border strip its envelope necessarily includes. A BUILDING, NOT A JURISDICTION: which agency answers at a given point is a service-area question this instance has not been researched for, so the card says where the nearest are and never who serves you. Nearest-three is a proximity fact, so for a reader near the state line the nearest one really may be in a neighbouring state, and the card's intro says these are straight-line distances.

anchor_point.note: New Hampshire State House, 107 North Main Street, Concord, Merrimack County

negative_point.note: The Gulf of Maine about 40 km east of Hampton Beach and 25 km south-east of the Isles of Shoals — outside New Hampshire and outside every other instance in the fleet, and inside permalink_gate so the app answers the click and every shipped layer correctly returns nothing. Measured 2026-11-11: TIGERweb's state layer names no state here (control: the State House in Concord returns New Hampshire), none of the state's shipped boundary files contains it, and no outline in fleet-outlines.json does. IT IS WATER, SO NO NEIGHBOUR'S GO-LIVE MOVES IT.

geometry.note: The whole-New Hampshire outline for the coverage wash (loadMetroOutline), dissolved from the county fabric (10 counties).
New Hampshire's 10 counties — the instance's offline anchor layer and the ground the coverage tests use.
The 2 U.S. House districts, TIGERweb layer 0 (CD120), the 2022 map, the same map as layer 4.
The 24 Senate districts, TIGERweb layer 1, the 2022 plan.
The 164 State House base districts, TIGERweb layer 2, the 2022 plan, each stamped with the floterial district over it (floterial, floterialOf) from NH GRANIT's floterial layer.

The ZIP code search index (scripts/build_zip_index.mjs): one Point per ZIP code the app's ZIP layer draws, at the spot inside it on the layer's own ground farthest from every edge, with its extent and its layer, so a ZIP code typed into the search box selects that spot, turns the ZIP layer on and pins it for comparison (ENGINE geocoder-search, showZip). A ZIP code with no spot 75 m clear of every edge is left out, and one that crosses into another app's state is listed by whichever app holds more of it. GENERATED from data/app/tiles/zip-code.pmtiles, with each spot inside metro-outline.json (the outline its coverage test reads); --check rebuilds it from the committed archive and outline. Exact count, because it changes only when the Census Bureau changes its ZIP Code Tabulation Areas, and that wants reading rather than a widened bound.

The officers New Hampshire elects statewide and its two U.S. senators: state, officers (office, name, the office's own website, the day the name was last checked there) and usSenate. Built weekly by scripts/build_statewide_officials.py from nh/data/source/statewide-officials.source.json, which lists each office, the name and the page that must print it; the build reads robots.txt before every page, refuses to write when a page it read no longer prints the name, keeps the last checked record when a page cannot be read, and takes the senators from senate.gov's own list. Network-first: a name can change.
